subject: golden retrievers
one_liner: Send tennis balls to the dogs you owe. Every dog you have ever sniffed will see the memo.
brand_voice_notes: A payments company that has fully accepted its customers cannot keep a secret or count past four. Copy is calm, compliance-adjacent and slightly tired. The currency is tennis balls (abbreviated TB), sticks are an unregulated secondary asset, and squirrels are treated as a recognised settlement risk. Never cute, never 'pupper'. Write it like a fintech that has filed a real S-1 and regrets some of it.

hero.h1: Every golden retriever owes somebody a tennis ball.
hero.sub: Ballpark is the payments app for golden retrievers. Split a stick, settle a debt, request your ball back from Murphy. Every transaction posts to a public feed, because no golden retriever has ever wanted privacy.

features.title: A public feed of everything
features.blurb: Every payment posts to a feed the whole dog park can read. Our research team asked 2,400 golden retrievers about privacy settings. All 2,400 wagged. We removed the settings.

features.title: Split the stick
features.blurb: Two dogs, one stick. Ballpark splits ownership to the centimetre and sends a payment request to whichever dog is currently chewing the other end.

features.title: Instant settlement, mostly
features.blurb: Balls arrive in under four seconds unless the recipient sees a squirrel, in which case the transfer is pending indefinitely. Ballpark does not insure against squirrels. Nobody does.

demo_screen_concept: A Ballpark wallet app on a phone-width column. Top: balance card showing '4 TB + 1 stick (disputed)', with Pay and Request buttons. Below: a public transaction feed of golden retrievers paying each other in tennis balls, each row with a round dog avatar, 'Murphy paid Biscuit', a memo like 'u know what for', an amount in TB, a timestamp like '2 sniffs ago', and a like/comment count. Tabs switch between Everyone / Friends / Mine, a search box filters dogs by name, tapping a heart likes the item, and the Pay/Request button opens a sheet where you pick a dog, set an amount with a +/- ball stepper, write a memo and send. The new payment slides into the top of the feed; if you request from Biscuit, a 'Squirrel detected. Settlement pending.' toast appears instead.

design_direction.style: Neubrutalist consumer-fintech, tennis-court daylight mode. A P2P wallet drawn with thick 3px ink outlines, flat fills and hard offset shadows on a warm cream ground, with golden fur and tennis-ball optic yellow as the only loud colours. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: masonry pins, iridescent gradients, crumb trails, lip buttons, lesson paths, bone meters, mascots in speech bubbles, wall labels, empty plinths, clay shadow stacks, silk threads, exuvia outlines, LCD greens, parts diagrams, warning boxes, rhumb lines, cartouches, wax seals, acorn marks, dot maps, terminal panels. Also absent: dark backgrounds, glassmorphism, serif type, paper textures, blurred shadows, gradients of any kind. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The feed row: features, testimonials and the hero mockup are written as Venmo-style feed items ('Murphy paid Biscuit 🎾 1'), each a white card with a 3px ink border and a 5px hard offset shadow. (2) The ball seam: a white curved tennis-ball seam drawn as an SVG path, used as section dividers and the loading glyph. (3) The TB amount pill: every number on the page is a rounded optic-yellow pill with an ink outline and tabular figures. (4) The court line: thin white double lines crossing the hero and pricing band, laid over a fur-gold field. Corners 14px on cards, 999px on pills and buttons. Shadows are hard 5px 5px 0 ink offsets only; buttons press into them on click.

fonts.body: 'Public Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Hero + social-proof feed + pricing + CTA, for a consumer P2P payments app
design_direction.motion_vocab: Hard, short and physical. Buttons translate 5px into their shadow on press (120ms). New feed items drop in from above with a small overshoot (220ms). The ball seam loader rotates once. All motion disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split hero. Left: huge Lexend Mega headline in ink on cream, sub in Public Sans, a gold 'Request a ball' button with hard shadow and a ghost 'open the demo' link. Right: a phone frame with a 3px ink border on a fur-gold panel crossed by white court lines, showing three stacked feed rows with avatar headshots and optic-yellow TB pills, slightly rotated -2deg.

images.rationale: Hero skipped: neubrutalist style and the hero is a drawn phone mockup, so a 16:9 photo would fight it. The demo is a social payments feed, which is photo-shaped (round profile avatars). Budget spent on 4 square headshots: 3 testimonial dogs (Murphy, Penny, Cooper) that double as feed avatars on both pages, plus Biscuit, the main counterparty in the demo feed.
